To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the H2 v=0-0 S lines in Orion Bar have a common spatial distribution, and that this distribution is not predicted by current PDR models.

The spatial distribution of H2 v =0-0 S1, v=0-0 S2, and v=1-0 S1 emission in the Orion Bar is remarkably well correlated, and the best-fit PDR model can account for this correlation, and for the observed intensities of the v=0-1 S1 and v=2-1 S1 lines.
the H2 rotational lines in the Orion Bar are consistent with a model that has a warm (T = 500 K), dense (n(H) = 10(5) cm(-3)) molecular layer 0.01 pc thick, located just behind the ionization front.

the H2 emission is not only spatially extended, but also has a complex temperature structure, and that a model with a simple temperature profile does not fit the data.
